NoteTexAccessor::wrap_display_math¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteTexAccessor::wrap_display_math(std::string_view delim) const

Wrap Each Cell As A Display Math Block¶

wrap_display_math() trims each cell and wraps it as a TeX display math block, inserting a newline between each delimiter and the content: open\ncontent\nclose. An empty delim defaults to \[/\]; the literal two-character delimiter "$$" is special-cased to $$/$$ (the same string on both sides); any other non-empty delim is used verbatim as both the opening and closing delimiter — there is no asymmetric open/close pairing for a custom delimiter, so a value such as "|" wraps as |\ncontent\n|, not a matched pair of distinct open/close characters.

This method does not check whether the cell already contains math delimiters. Contrast this directly with wrap_inline_math, which skips a cell that already has a $, \(, or \[ anywhere in it: wrap_display_math() always wraps a non-empty cell, even one that is already $already$ — the existing dollar signs end up nested one level inside the new outer delimiters. A cell that is empty after trimming is returned empty, with no delimiters added.

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. Undefined input remains undefined; Bool, Int64, Float64, and Bytes receivers are rejected because TeX source is Text.

Example 1: Default Delimiter, Empty Cell, And Unconditional Wrapping¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"x+y", "", "$already$"})
              .tex().wrap_display_math("")
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["\\[\nx+y\n\\]", "", "\\[\n$already$\n\\]"]

The empty second cell stays empty. The third cell, already containing $ delimiters, is still wrapped — unlike wrap_inline_math, there is no existing-math check here.

Example 2: The "$$" Special Case¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"x+y"}).tex().wrap_display_math("$$") << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["$$\nx+y\n$$"]

Example 3: A Custom Delimiter Is Used On Both Sides¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"x+y"}).tex().wrap_display_math("~") << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["~\nx+y\n~"]

~ is not paired with a distinct closing character; the same delimiter opens and closes.

Example 4: Undefined And Non-Text Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().wrap_display_math("").defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().wrap_display_math("");
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "wrap display math Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
wrap display math Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • wrap_inline_math: the inline counterpart, which skips cells that already contain a math delimiter.

  • add_math_delimiters: choose inline or display wrapping automatically per cell instead of committing to one form.

  • balance_math_delims: repair unbalanced delimiters already present, rather than adding new ones.
